# Public Star Driving School: full site content

Source: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/ . Generated 2026-11-14. Prices are in Canadian dollars; HST is 13%.

Public Star Driving School is an MTO-approved driving school in Ajax, Ontario, Canada, offering one-on-one G2 and G driving lessons, road test packages and the Beginner Driver Education (BDE) course with free pick-up and drop-off in Scarborough, North York, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa. G2 lessons start at $50/hour + HST ($56.50) and G lessons at $60/hour + HST ($67.80).

## Key facts

- Business name: Public Star Driving School
- Type: Driving school (MTO-approved Beginner Driver Education provider)
- Address: 9 Graywardine Ln, Ajax, ON L1Z 0R9, Canada
- Phone (call or text): (437) 777-4494
- Email: publicstardrivingschool@gmail.com
- Website and online booking: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/#book
- Hours: 7 days a week, 8am to 9pm
- Service areas: Scarborough, North York, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby, Oshawa (east GTA and Durham Region, Ontario)
- Nearby DriveTest centres we train for: Metro East (Scarborough), Port Union (Scarborough), Downsview (North York), Oshawa
- Lessons: one-on-one, in dual-brake insured cars, free pick-up and drop-off at home, school or work
- Road test packages include use of the instructor's car and a warm-up lesson
- Help booking DriveTest road test appointments
- Lessons available in more than one language; ask when booking
- No payment needed to request a booking

- Basic: $499 + HST ($563.87 total). Everything you need to earn your BDE certificate. Includes: 20 hrs online theory (self-paced); 10 hrs one-on-one in-car lessons; 10 hrs homelink assignments; Defensive driving & intersection techniques; Road test preparation; MTO certificate processing; Free pick-up & drop-off.
- Premium: $649 + HST ($733.37 total). Extra practice plus our car for your road test. Includes: Everything in Basic; 11 hrs one-on-one in-car lessons; Use of instructor's car for G2 road test; Road test booking assistance; Free pick-up & drop-off.
- Advanced: $799 + HST ($902.87 total). Maximum preparation for nervous or first-time drivers. Includes: Everything in Premium; 15 hrs one-on-one in-car lessons; Use of instructor's car for G2 road test; Road test booking assistance; Free pick-up & drop-off.

## Frequently asked questions

Q: Do I need to complete the full BDE course to take lessons?
A: No. If you already have a G1 or G2, you can book individual lessons or an hours-plus-road-test bundle without enrolling in the full course.

Q: What does the BDE certificate get me?
A: Graduating from a Ministry-approved BDE course lets you take your G2 road test after 8 months instead of 12, and most insurers offer a discount for new drivers who complete it.

Q: Can I use your car for my road test?
A: Yes. Every hours-plus-road-test bundle and the Premium and Advanced BDE packages include the use of the instructor's car on test day, along with a warm-up lesson beforehand.

Q: How do pick-up and drop-off work?
A: Your instructor picks you up from your home, school or workplace within our service area and drops you off at the end of the lesson, at no extra charge.

Q: How do I pay?
A: No payment is required to request a booking. We'll confirm your schedule first and arrange payment by e-transfer or in person before your first lesson.

Q: Can I book my DriveTest appointment through you?
A: Yes. We'll help you find and book an available road test slot at the DriveTest centre closest to you.

# G2 Licence Rules and Restrictions in Ontario: What You Can and Cannot Do

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/g2-licence-rules-ontario/
Published: 2026-11-14. Updated: 2026-11-14.

Quick answer: With a G2 licence in Ontario you can drive alone on all roads, including 400-series highways, at any time of day, but you must keep a zero blood alcohol level, have no drugs in your system and carry only as many passengers as there are working seatbelts. If you are 19 or under, between midnight and 5 a.m. you can carry only one passenger aged 19 or under in your first six months on a G2, and up to three after that. Breaking G2 rules can bring a 30 day suspension for a first offence, 90 days for a second, and loss of your novice licence for a third.

Passing your G2 road test is a big moment: for the first time, you can drive without an experienced driver beside you. But a G2 is still a novice licence, and Ontario keeps several rules in place until you pass your G test. This guide explains every G2 restriction, what happens if you break one, and how to get through the 12 months safely. It is written for new drivers in Scarborough, North York, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa, but the rules apply across Ontario.

All of the rules below come from ontario.ca (https://www.ontario.ca/page/get-g-drivers-licence-new-drivers) and are current as of November 2026. Rules can change, so check the official pages if you are unsure.

## What can you do with a G2 licence in Ontario?

Compared with a G1, a G2 gives you a lot more freedom. Ontario says G2 drivers can drive:

- without another experienced driver in the car,
- on all Ontario roads, including 400-series highways and high-speed expressways,
- at any time of the day, in most cases.

That is why the G2 stage is the best time to build real highway experience before your G test. Our G road test highway tips (/blog/g-road-test-highway-tips/) explain what to practise.

## G2 restrictions at a glance

| Rule | Who it applies to |
| --- | --- |
| Zero blood alcohol level | All G2 drivers |
| No drugs, including cannabis, in your system | All G2 drivers |
| Only as many passengers as working seatbelts | All G2 drivers |
| Midnight to 5 a.m.: only one passenger aged 19 or under (first six months) | G2 drivers aged 19 or under |
| Midnight to 5 a.m.: up to three passengers aged 19 or under (after six months) | G2 drivers aged 19 or under |
| No hand-held phone use while driving | All drivers, with tougher penalties for novices |

## Zero tolerance for alcohol and drugs

Ontario's zero tolerance law says you cannot have any alcohol in your system if you hold a G1, G2, M1 or M2 licence, at any age. The same applies to all drivers aged 21 or under, even with a full G. The rule also covers cannabis and other drugs: Ontario says young and novice drivers must have no alcohol and no drugs in their system when they drive.

Ontario lists these penalties for young and novice drivers who break zero tolerance, on top of any other impaired driving charges:

| Offence | Immediate suspension | Penalty | Other |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First time | 7 days | $250 | 8 hour education course |
| Second time | 14 days | $350 | 16 hour treatment program |
| Third time | 30 days | $450 | 16 hour treatment program and a 6 month ignition interlock |

If you are convicted, the fine can be $60 to $1,000, and your licence can be suspended for a further 30 or 90 days or cancelled. A reinstatement fee also applies each time a licence is suspended. The simple answer: if you have had anything at all, do not drive.

## G2 passenger rules

Every G2 driver must carry only as many passengers as there are working seatbelts. No exceptions.

If you are 19 or under, there is an extra rule between midnight and 5 a.m.:

1. First six months on your G2: only one passenger aged 19 or under.
2. After six months: up to three passengers aged 19 or under.

These late-night limits do not apply if a fully licensed driver with at least four years of experience is in the car, or if your passengers are immediate family members, such as a brother or sister.

## Phones and distracted driving on a G2

Ontario's distracted driving law applies to everyone, but novice drivers face harsher consequences. You cannot hold a phone or other device while driving, including when you are stopped in traffic or at a red light. You can use a hands-free device only to turn it on and off, and a mounted phone only to touch a button to make, answer or end a call.

The fine is $615 if settled out of court, and more if you are summoned to court. Novice drivers do not get demerit points for this offence. Instead, Ontario says G1 and G2 drivers face:

- a 30 day licence suspension for a first conviction,
- a 90 day licence suspension for a second conviction,
- cancellation of your licence and removal from the graduated licensing system for a third conviction, which means starting over.

Set your GPS and music before you pull out, and put your phone out of reach.

## Demerit points for G2 drivers

Novice drivers reach suspension much sooner than fully licensed drivers. According to Ontario's demerit point page (https://www.ontario.ca/page/understanding-demerit-points):

| Demerit points | What happens to a novice driver |
| --- | --- |
| 2 to 5 | Warning letter |
| 6 to 8 | Second warning letter |
| 9 or more | 60 day licence suspension |

Points stay on your record for two years from the offence date. A fully licensed driver, by comparison, is not suspended until 15 points.

## Escalating penalties for novice drivers

Ontario also has escalating penalties for G1 and G2 drivers who are convicted of breaking graduated licensing rules, or of a Highway Traffic Act offence worth four or more demerit points:

- First offence: 30 day suspension.
- Second offence: 90 day suspension.
- Third offence: you lose your novice licence and must start again, taking all tests and paying all fees. You also lose any time credit, including the time saved from a driver education course.

Losing your G2 can set you back many months, so these rules are worth taking seriously.

## How long do you keep a G2?

You hold your G2 for at least 12 months before you can take the G road test. Ontario gives you up to five years to finish the whole process from G1 to G, or you have to start over. Our G1 to G licence timeline (/blog/g1-to-g-licence-timeline-ontario/) shows how the dates fit together, and the G2 vs G road test (/blog/g2-vs-g-road-test/) comparison explains what the next test adds.

## Tips for a smooth G2 year

- Drive often, not just on weekends. The 12 months are meant for experience, so use them.
- Get highway practice early. Start with quiet times on the 401 or 412 before rush hour.
- Keep a clean record. Even two demerit points trigger a warning letter.
- Plan late-night trips. If you are 19 or under, count passengers before you leave after midnight.
- Book a refresher before your G test. A lesson or two helps you fix habits that crept in.

If you want help, our G lessons start at $60 + HST ($67.80) an hour, and our 3 hours + road test G package is $300 + HST ($339.00), which includes our car for the test and a warm-up drive. Still waiting for your G2 test? Read how to pass the G2 road test on the first try (/blog/how-to-pass-g2-road-test/) and the G2 automatic fails list (/blog/g2-road-test-automatic-fails/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I drive on the highway with a G2 in Ontario?

Yes. G2 drivers can drive on all Ontario roads, including 400-series highways and high-speed expressways, without another driver in the car.

### Can a G2 driver drink any alcohol before driving?

No. G2 drivers must keep a zero blood alcohol level and have no drugs, including cannabis, in their system.

### How many passengers can I have with a G2?

Only as many as there are working seatbelts. If you are 19 or under, between midnight and 5 a.m. you can carry one passenger aged 19 or under in your first six months, and up to three after that, unless an experienced driver is with you or the passengers are immediate family.

### What happens if I get caught on my phone with a G2?

You face a $615 fine if settled out of court and a 30 day suspension for a first conviction, 90 days for a second, and cancellation of your licence for a third.

### How many demerit points can a G2 driver have?

A warning letter comes at 2 points, a second at 6, and a 60 day suspension at 9 or more.

# Converting a Foreign Driver's Licence in Ontario: A Newcomer's Guide

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/foreign-licence-exchange-ontario/
Published: 2026-11-13. Updated: 2026-11-13.

Quick answer: You can drive in Ontario on a valid licence from another country for 60 days, and after that you need an Ontario licence. If your licence is from another Canadian province, a U.S. state or one of the countries with an exchange agreement (such as Australia, France, Germany, Great Britain, Japan, South Korea or Ukraine), you can apply to exchange it at a DriveTest centre. From any other country, you take the vision test, knowledge test and G2 road test, wait at least 12 months, then take the G road test, and you can get credit for up to one year of driving experience with a valid foreign licence and a letter of authentication.

Moving to Ontario comes with a long to-do list, and getting the right driver's licence is near the top for most newcomers. The good news: your driving experience back home still counts for something. How much it counts depends on where your licence comes from. This guide walks through the rules as ontario.ca explains them, plus what we see helps newcomers pass their road tests in Ajax, Scarborough and across Durham Region.

## How long can you drive in Ontario on a foreign licence?

According to ontario.ca, you can use a valid licence from another province, state or country for 60 days. After 60 days, you need to switch to an Ontario driver's licence.

Sixty days goes by quickly when you are also finding a home, a job and a school for your kids. Start the licence process in your first few weeks, especially if you will need to book road tests.

## Which countries can exchange their licence in Ontario?

Ontario lets you exchange an out-of-province licence if you are relocating from:

- any Canadian province or territory
- the Canadian Armed Forces
- a U.S. state (U.S. territories and protectorates are not included)
- Australia, Austria, Belgium, Croatia, Denmark, France, Germany, Great Britain, Hungary, the Isle of Man, Japan, South Korea, Kosovo, New Zealand, Northern Ireland, the Republic of Ireland, Switzerland, Taiwan or Ukraine

Even from one of these places, the exchange is not automatic. Ontario says the process depends on where you were licensed, your licence class and your driving experience, and that you might still need to take a knowledge test or road test. Check the exchange details on drivetest.ca for your exact situation before you go.

## What if your country is not on the exchange list?

Most newcomers to the Greater Toronto Area come from countries without an exchange agreement, including India, Pakistan, the Philippines, China, Iran, Nigeria and many others. If that is you, ontario.ca lists these steps:

1. Pass the vision test and the knowledge test at a DriveTest centre.
2. Pass the G2 road test.
3. Wait at least 12 months before you attempt the G road test.
4. Pass the G road test to get your full G licence.

Since July 1, 2026, you can get credit for up to one year of driving experience by showing a valid, original foreign driver's licence and an authentication document. Ask DriveTest how that credit applies to your timeline when you apply.

For a full picture of how the levels fit together, see our G1 to G licence timeline (/blog/g1-to-g-licence-timeline-ontario/).

## What is a letter of authentication?

To get credit for your foreign experience, you need a letter of authentication. Ontario says it must be:

- an official letter from the foreign government or agency that issued your licence
- a confirmation that your licence is authentic
- written in English or French

Request this letter early. Depending on the country, it can take weeks to arrive, and you may need family back home to help.

## Documents to bring to DriveTest

You apply in person at a DriveTest centre or at ServiceOntario Bay and College in Toronto. Bring:

| Document | Notes from ontario.ca |
| --- | --- |
| Identity documents | Originals showing your legal name and date of birth |
| Foreign driver's licence | Original and valid, with a visible expiry date |
| Translation | Needed if the licence is not in English or French |
| Letter of authentication | Needed to get credit for driving experience |
| Proof of driving experience | Original supporting documents in English or French |

Translations: the translation must be done by a certified translator and dated within six months of your application. Ontario accepts translations from non-Canadian embassies, consulates or high commissioner's offices, but not other translators from the country that issued the licence. Translators must provide proof of their credentials.

Since May 11, 2026, Class G applicants also declare that Ontario is their primary place of residence and that their presence in Canada is legal.

DriveTest charges fees for the licence application, the knowledge test and each road test. Check the current list on drivetest.ca before you go, since we cannot confirm amounts here.

## Why experienced drivers still fail the Ontario road test

This is the part that surprises many newcomers. You may have driven safely for years, yet Ontario examiners mark specific habits that are normal elsewhere. The ones we see most often:

- Rolling stops. Ontario expects a full stop behind the line at every stop sign.
- Shoulder checks. Examiners watch for a head turn before every lane change, merge and turn from the curb. Mirrors alone are not enough.
- Right turns on red. They are allowed, but only after a complete stop and when it is safe.
- School buses and pedestrians. The rules around stopped school buses and crosswalks are strict.
- Speed in school zones and residential streets. Posted limits change often, and examiners notice.

None of this is hard to fix, but old habits are automatic. A few lessons with an instructor who knows the test routes usually clears them up. Our G2 automatic fails list (/blog/g2-road-test-automatic-fails/) covers the mistakes that end a test early.

## How many lessons does an experienced newcomer need?

Less than a brand new driver, in most cases. Experienced drivers often need only a couple of hours to learn Ontario test habits, then a run through the test route. Our guide on how many lessons you need before the G2 (/blog/how-many-driving-lessons-before-g2/) goes into more detail.

Here are our packages that newcomers book most often (prices include 13% HST):

| Package | Price | Total with HST |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G2: 1 hour lesson | $50 | $56.50 |
| G2: 2 hours + road test | $200 | $226.00 |
| G2: 5 hours + road test | $330 | $372.90 |
| G: 2 hours + road test | $250 | $282.50 |
| G: 3 hours + road test | $300 | $339.00 |

Road test packages include the use of our car on test day. If you do not own a car in Canada yet, that matters: see renting a car for your road test (/blog/road-test-car-rental-ontario/). We offer free pick-up and drop-off in Ajax, Pickering, Whitby, Oshawa, Scarborough and North York.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I drive in Ontario with an international driving permit?

Ontario's exchange page says you can drive on a valid licence from another country for 60 days, then you need an Ontario licence. It does not describe the international driving permit, so check with DriveTest or your insurer about your situation.

### Is India on Ontario's licence exchange list?

No. India is not on the list ontario.ca gives. Drivers from India take the vision test, knowledge test and G2 road test, and can get credit for up to one year of experience with a valid licence and a letter of authentication.

### Do I need to take the knowledge test if I have driven for years?

If your licence is from a country without an exchange agreement, yes. Ontario lists the vision test and knowledge test as the first steps. Drivers from exchange countries may or may not need tests, depending on their circumstances.

### Where can I get my licence translated?

Ontario accepts translations from a certified translator, including non-Canadian embassies, consulates and high commissioner's offices. The translation must be dated within six months of your application.

### Can I use a driving school car for my road test?

Yes. All our road test packages include the car on test day, plus a warm-up lesson before the test.

# Driving Lessons in North York: A Guide for New Drivers

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/driving-lessons-north-york/
Published: 2026-11-12. Updated: 2026-11-12.

Quick answer: Driving lessons in North York are one-on-one sessions with a certified instructor who picks you up from home, school or work and builds from quiet residential streets up to Yonge Street, Sheppard Avenue and Highway 401. At Public Star, a single G2 lesson is $50 + HST ($56.50), a G lesson is $60 + HST ($67.80), and the G2 5 hours plus road test bundle is $330 + HST ($372.90), including a warm-up and our car on test day.

North York is the busiest of the six cities our instructors teach in. It has some of the heaviest traffic in Ontario, a stretch of Highway 401 that many new drivers find intimidating, and plenty of quiet side streets where you can learn the basics first. This guide explains how lessons in North York work, which roads help you prepare for your road test and what it all costs.

## What does a driving lesson in North York look like?

Every lesson is one-on-one, so the full hour is yours. Your instructor picks you up from your home, school or workplace in North York, whether that is near York University, a subway station on Yonge Street or a quiet street in Don Mills, and plans each lesson around what you need next.

Your first lesson usually includes:

- Getting set up: seat, mirrors and steering wheel position before you move.
- A quick assessment: starts, stops, turns and lane position on quiet streets.
- Honest feedback: what you already do well and which habits would cost marks on a road test.
- A plan: a realistic estimate of how many lessons you need and what each one will cover.

Each lesson after that builds on the last one. In North York, that usually means extra time on the skills busy city traffic demands: scanning for pedestrians and cyclists, choosing the right lane early and making left turns at large intersections without rushing.

## What licence do you need to start lessons in North York?

You need a G1 licence, which you get by passing a vision test and the written knowledge test at a DriveTest centre. Once you have it, you can start lessons with a certified driving instructor right away.

While you hold a G1 in Ontario, you must:

- Keep a zero blood alcohol level.
- Not drive between midnight and 5 a.m.
- Not drive on 400-series highways or high-speed expressways such as the 401.
- Always drive with a fully licensed driver who has at least four years of driving experience, and who is the only other person in the front seat.

There is one important exception. When you drive with a driving instructor certified in Ontario, you can drive on any road. For North York drivers that matters a lot, because Highway 401, Highway 404 and the Don Valley Parkway all run through or beside the city. A lesson is the only way to practise on them while you hold a G1.

## Local roads worth practising on in North York

North York packs almost every kind of driving into a small area. Lessons usually move through it in stages:

| Stage | Type of road | What you practise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Beginner | Residential streets in neighbourhoods like Willowdale, Bayview Village and Newtonbrook | Steering control, full stops, speed control, scanning for children and pedestrians |
| Building up | Main roads such as Bathurst Street, Bayview Avenue and Leslie Street | Left turns at lights, lane changes, following distance |
| Busier traffic | Yonge Street, Sheppard Avenue and Finch Avenue | Heavy traffic, buses, plaza entrances, pedestrians and cyclists |
| G test prep | Highway 401, Highway 404 and the Don Valley Parkway | Merging, exiting and changing lanes at highway speed |

DriveTest does not publish its test routes, so memorizing streets is not the goal. The goal is to feel calm on every type of road, so nothing on test day feels new. A driver who can handle Yonge and Sheppard at rush hour is usually well prepared for any test route.

## Driving on Highway 401 through North York

The 401 through North York has express and collector lanes, frequent exits and heavy traffic for much of the day. For a G road test, you need to merge, change lanes and exit smoothly at highway speed. We start highway practice only once you are comfortable on busy city roads, and we usually begin outside rush hour.

The skills we focus on:

1. Building speed on the ramp so you merge at the speed of traffic, not below it.
2. Checking mirrors and blind spots before every lane change, every time.
3. Planning exits early so you are in the correct lane well before the ramp.
4. Keeping a safe following distance even when other drivers do not.

Our G road test highway tips (/blog/g-road-test-highway-tips/) go through the full checklist examiners look for.

## Where do North York drivers take their road test?

There are several DriveTest centres across Toronto, and North York students book whichever one has a date that suits them. Some of our students choose Metro East in Scarborough, where we teach often. Check the current list of centres and available dates on drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca/), since availability changes often.

Whichever centre you pick, it helps to spend your last lesson on the roads around it. Our guide to Metro East DriveTest (/blog/metro-east-drivetest-tips/) covers that centre in detail.

## How many lessons will you need?

Ontario does not set a minimum number of lessons. It does set waiting periods: you must hold your G1 for 12 months before your G2 road test, or 8 months if you finish a government-approved driver education course. After that, you hold your G2 for 12 months before you can take the G road test.

As a rough guide for North York students:

1. Confident drivers who practise often with family usually need 2 to 3 hours of test-focused lessons.
2. Drivers who still hesitate at left turns, lane changes or busy intersections usually need 4 to 5 hours.
3. Complete beginners do best with 10 hours or a full BDE course.

For the signs that you are ready to book, read how many driving lessons you need before your G2 (/blog/how-many-driving-lessons-before-g2/). To see the whole path from G1 to a full licence, our G1 to G timeline (/blog/g1-to-g-licence-timeline-ontario/) lays it out step by step.

These are Public Star's current prices. HST is 13%, and the total is in brackets.

| Package | Price |

| G2 1 hour lesson | $50 + HST ($56.50) |
| G2 3 hours + road test | $250 + HST ($282.50) |
| G2 5 hours + road test | $330 + HST ($372.90) |
| G2 10 hours + road test | $550 + HST ($621.50) |
| G 1 hour lesson | $60 + HST ($67.80) |
| G 3 hours + road test | $300 + HST ($339.00) |
| G 5 hours + road test | $400 + HST ($452.00) |
| BDE Basic | $499 + HST ($563.87) |
| BDE Premium | $649 + HST ($733.37) |
| BDE Advanced | $799 + HST ($902.87) |

Every hours plus road test bundle includes a warm-up before your test and the use of our instructor's car on test day. The road test fee itself is paid to DriveTest and is not included; check the current amount on drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca/tests/fees/). For every package, see our driving lesson price guide (/blog/driving-lessons-cost-ontario/).

## Is the BDE course worth it for North York drivers?

A government-approved BDE course lets you take your G2 road test after 8 months instead of 12. Many insurers also offer a discount to new drivers who complete one, so ask your insurance company before you decide. Our BDE packages combine online theory with one-on-one in-car lessons in North York and the surrounding area. Read whether the BDE course is worth it (/blog/is-bde-course-worth-it/) for a fuller comparison.

## Tips for getting the most out of your lessons

- Practise between lessons. Even 20 minutes on quiet streets helps new skills stick.
- Learn to expect the unexpected. Pedestrians, cyclists and buses pulling out are part of every North York drive, so keep scanning.
- Ask questions. Your instructor would rather explain a right of way rule twice than watch you guess on test day.
- Know the common mistakes. Read our list of G2 road test automatic fails (/blog/g2-road-test-automatic-fails/) before you book.

## Do you teach outside North York?

Yes. We are based in Ajax, and our instructors also teach in Scarborough, Pickering, Whitby and Oshawa, with free pick-up and drop-off within our service area. If you live east of North York, our guides to driving lessons in Pickering (/blog/driving-lessons-pickering/) and driving lessons in Ajax (/blog/driving-lessons-ajax/) cover those cities too.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do you offer pick-up in North York?

Yes. Your instructor picks you up from your home, school or workplace in North York and drops you off after the lesson at no extra charge.

### Can I practise on Highway 401 with a G1?

Only with a certified driving instructor. G1 drivers cannot use 400-series highways with a family member, but when you drive with an instructor certified in Ontario, you can drive on any road.

### Which DriveTest centre should I book from North York?

Book whichever Toronto-area centre has a date that works for you, and check drivetest.ca for current openings. Then plan a lesson on the roads around that centre before test day.

### Can I use your car for my road test?

Yes. Every hours plus road test bundle, and the Premium and Advanced BDE packages, include the use of our car on test day along with a warm-up beforehand.

### Can I take lessons without signing up for BDE?

Yes. You can book a single lesson or an hours plus road test bundle as soon as you have your G1.

# Driving Lessons in Oshawa: A Guide for New Drivers

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/driving-lessons-oshawa/
Published: 2026-11-11. Updated: 2026-11-11.

Quick answer: Driving lessons in Oshawa are one-on-one sessions with a certified instructor who picks you up from home, school or work and builds from quiet residential streets up to downtown Oshawa, Simcoe Street and Highway 401. At Public Star, a single G2 lesson is $50 + HST ($56.50), a G lesson is $60 + HST ($67.80), and the G2 5 hours plus road test bundle is $330 + HST ($372.90), including a warm-up and our car on test day.

Oshawa is one of the six cities our instructors teach in every week, a short drive east of our home base in Ajax. It is also home to the Oshawa DriveTest centre, which many Durham Region students choose for their road test. Whether you just passed your G1 knowledge test or you are getting ready for your G2 or G road test, this guide explains how lessons in Oshawa work, which local roads help you prepare and what it all costs.

## What does a driving lesson in Oshawa look like?

Every lesson is one-on-one, so the full hour is yours. Your instructor picks you up from your home, school or workplace in Oshawa, including the Durham College and Ontario Tech University area in the north end, and plans each lesson around what you need next.

Your first lesson usually includes:

- Getting set up: seat, mirrors and steering wheel position before you move.
- A quick assessment: starts, stops, turns and lane position on quiet streets.
- Honest feedback: what you already do well and which habits would cost marks on a road test.
- A plan: a realistic estimate of how many lessons you need and what each one will cover.

Each lesson after that builds on the last one, with extra time on the skills family practice often misses, such as complete stops, shoulder checks and smooth lane changes.

## What licence do you need to start lessons in Oshawa?

You need a G1 licence, which you get by passing a vision test and the written knowledge test at a DriveTest centre. Once you have it, you can start lessons with a certified driving instructor right away.

While you hold a G1 in Ontario, you must:

- Keep a zero blood alcohol level.
- Not drive between midnight and 5 a.m.
- Not drive on 400-series highways or high-speed expressways such as the 401.
- Always drive with a fully licensed driver who has at least four years of driving experience, and who is the only other person in the front seat.

There is one important exception. When you drive with a driving instructor certified in Ontario, you can drive on any road. For Oshawa drivers that matters, because Highway 401 runs along the south end of the city and Highway 407 crosses the north. A lesson is the only way to practise on them while you hold a G1.

## Local roads worth practising on in Oshawa

Oshawa has quiet subdivisions, a downtown with one-way streets, wide arterial roads and two highways, all within a few minutes of each other. Lessons usually move through them in stages:

| Stage | Type of road | What you practise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Beginner | Residential streets in neighbourhoods like Windfields, Samac and Eastdale | Steering control, full stops, speed control, scanning for pedestrians |
| Building up | Main roads such as Ritson Road, Harmony Road and Stevenson Road | Left turns at lights, lane changes, following distance |
| Busier traffic | Downtown Oshawa, Simcoe Street and Taunton Road | One-way streets, buses, plaza entrances and pedestrians |
| G test prep | Highway 401 and Highway 407 | Merging, exiting and changing lanes at highway speed |

DriveTest does not publish its test routes, so memorizing streets is not the goal. The goal is to feel comfortable on every type of road, so nothing on test day feels new.

## Where do Oshawa drivers take their road test?

Most Oshawa students book the Oshawa DriveTest centre in Midtown Mall, because it is close to home and the surrounding roads are the ones they already practise on. Some book Metro East or Port Union in Scarborough when those centres have earlier openings. Check the current list of centres and available dates on drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca/), since availability changes often.

Our Oshawa DriveTest tips (/blog/oshawa-drivetest-tips/) cover the centre itself: where it is, what happens when you check in and how to prepare for the roads around it. If you are thinking about Scarborough instead, read our guide to Metro East DriveTest (/blog/metro-east-drivetest-tips/).

## How many lessons will you need?

Ontario does not set a minimum number of lessons. It does set waiting periods: you must hold your G1 for 12 months before your G2 road test, or 8 months if you finish a government-approved driver education course. After that, you hold your G2 for 12 months before you can take the G road test.

As a rough guide for Oshawa students:

1. Confident drivers who practise often with family usually need 2 to 3 hours of test-focused lessons.
2. Drivers who still hesitate at left turns, lane changes or busy intersections usually need 4 to 5 hours.
3. Complete beginners do best with 10 hours or a full BDE course.

For the signs that you are ready to book, read how many driving lessons you need before your G2 (/blog/how-many-driving-lessons-before-g2/). To see the whole path from G1 to a full licence, our G1 to G timeline (/blog/g1-to-g-licence-timeline-ontario/) lays it out step by step.

## How much do driving lessons cost in Oshawa?

These are Public Star's current prices. HST is 13%, and the total is in brackets.

| Package | Price |
| --- | --- |
| G2 1 hour lesson | $50 + HST ($56.50) |
| G2 3 hours + road test | $250 + HST ($282.50) |
| G2 5 hours + road test | $330 + HST ($372.90) |
| G2 10 hours + road test | $550 + HST ($621.50) |
| G 1 hour lesson | $60 + HST ($67.80) |
| G 3 hours + road test | $300 + HST ($339.00) |
| G 5 hours + road test | $400 + HST ($452.00) |
| BDE Basic | $499 + HST ($563.87) |
| BDE Premium | $649 + HST ($733.37) |
| BDE Advanced | $799 + HST ($902.87) |

Every hours plus road test bundle includes a warm-up before your test and the use of our instructor's car on test day. The road test fee itself is paid to DriveTest and is not included; check the current amount on drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca/tests/fees/). For every package, see our driving lesson price guide (/blog/driving-lessons-cost-ontario/).

## Is the BDE course worth it for Oshawa drivers?

A government-approved BDE course lets you take your G2 road test after 8 months instead of 12. Many insurers also offer a discount to new drivers who complete one, so ask your insurance company before you decide. Our BDE packages combine online theory with one-on-one in-car lessons in Oshawa and the surrounding area. Read whether the BDE course is worth it (/blog/is-bde-course-worth-it/) for a fuller comparison.

## Tips for getting the most out of your lessons

- Practise between lessons. Even 20 minutes on quiet streets helps new skills stick.
- Get used to one-way streets. Downtown Oshawa is a good place to practise lane choice and turning from the correct lane.
- Ask questions. Your instructor would rather explain a right of way rule twice than watch you guess on test day.
- Know the common mistakes. Read our list of G2 road test automatic fails (/blog/g2-road-test-automatic-fails/), and for the G test, our highway tips (/blog/g-road-test-highway-tips/).

## Do you teach outside Oshawa?

Yes. We are based in Ajax, and our instructors also teach in Pickering, Whitby, Oshawa, Scarborough and North York, with free pick-up and drop-off within our service area. If you live nearby, our guides to driving lessons in Whitby (/blog/driving-lessons-whitby/) and driving lessons in Ajax (/blog/driving-lessons-ajax/) cover those cities too.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do you offer pick-up in Oshawa?

Yes. Your instructor picks you up from your home, school or workplace in Oshawa and drops you off after the lesson at no extra charge.

### Can I practise on Highway 401 with a G1?

Only with a certified driving instructor. G1 drivers cannot use 400-series highways with a family member, but when you drive with an instructor certified in Ontario, you can drive on any road.

### Where is the DriveTest centre in Oshawa?

DriveTest lists the Oshawa centre in Midtown Mall at 200 John St W. Check drivetest.ca for current hours and open dates before you book.

### Can I use your car for my road test?

Yes. Every hours plus road test bundle, and the Premium and Advanced BDE packages, include the use of our car on test day along with a warm-up beforehand.

### Can I take lessons without signing up for BDE?

Yes. You can book a single lesson or an hours plus road test bundle as soon as you have your G1.

# Driving Lessons in Ajax: What to Expect

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/driving-lessons-ajax/
Published: 2026-11-08. Updated: 2026-11-08.

Quick answer: Driving lessons in Ajax are one-on-one sessions with a certified instructor who picks you up from home, school or work, starting with an assessment and moving on to the skills on your road test. At Public Star, a single G2 lesson is $50 + HST ($56.50) and a G lesson is $60 + HST ($67.80), and hours plus road test bundles include a warm-up and the use of our car on test day.

Public Star Driving School is based in Ajax, so this is the town our instructors know best. If you are a new driver here, or you are getting ready for your G2 or G road test, this guide explains what a lesson actually looks like, which local roads are worth practising on, where Ajax drivers usually take their road test, and what it costs.

## What happens in your first driving lesson in Ajax?

Your first lesson is mostly about finding out where you are. Your instructor picks you up from your home, school or workplace and starts on quiet residential streets before moving to busier roads once you are comfortable.

During that first hour, expect to:

- Adjust the car properly: seat, mirrors and steering wheel, before you move.
- Show what you can already do: smooth starts and stops, turns, and lane position.
- Get honest feedback: a short list of what you do well and what needs work.
- Agree on a plan: how many lessons you likely need and what each one will cover.

If you have never driven before, the first lesson stays in quiet areas. If you already practise with family, your instructor will move quickly to the things that cost marks on a road test.

## What do you need before you can book a lesson?

You need at least a G1 licence. Ontario gives you a G1 after you pass the vision test and the written knowledge test at a DriveTest centre. With a G1, you can drive with a certified driving instructor, and lessons are a good way to start safely.

Remember that G1 drivers must:

- Keep a zero blood alcohol level.
- Not drive between midnight and 5 a.m.
- Not drive on 400-series highways or high-speed expressways, unless you are with a driving instructor certified in Ontario.
- Always drive with a fully licensed driver who has at least four years of driving experience.

That third rule matters in Ajax, because Highway 401 runs right through town. With a certified instructor, you can practise highway merging before you are allowed to do it with family.

## Local roads worth practising on in Ajax

Ajax has a good mix of the roads you will see on a road test: quiet crescents, school zones, busy arterial roads and highway ramps. Lessons usually build up through them in this order:

| Stage | Type of road | What you practise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Beginner | Residential streets and crescents | Steering, full stops, speed control, watching for pedestrians |
| Building up | Main roads such as Harwood Avenue, Westney Road and Salem Road | Lane changes, left turns at lights, following distance |
| Busier traffic | Kingston Road and Bayly Street | Multi-lane driving, plazas, buses and turning traffic |
| G test prep | Highway 401 | Merging, exiting, lane changes at highway speed |

DriveTest does not publish its road test routes, so the goal is not to memorize streets. It is to get comfortable with every type of road, so nothing on test day surprises you.

## Where do Ajax drivers take their road test?

Most Ajax drivers book their road test at a nearby centre. Popular choices for our students are Oshawa and Metro East in Scarborough, and some book Port Union. Check the full list of centres and available dates on drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca/).

The best centre is the one whose roads you can practise on. Our guides to Oshawa DriveTest (/blog/oshawa-drivetest-tips/) and Metro East DriveTest (/blog/metro-east-drivetest-tips/) describe each area and what to expect when you check in. If you are not sure which to pick, we can help you find and book an available slot at the centre closest to you.

## How many lessons will you need?

It depends on how much you have already driven. Ontario does not require a minimum number of lessons. You must hold your G1 for 12 months before your G2 road test, or 8 months if you finish a government-approved driver education course.

As a rough guide:

1. Confident drivers who practise often with family usually need 2 to 3 hours, focused on test skills.
2. Drivers who still hesitate at left turns or lane changes usually need 4 to 5 hours.
3. Complete beginners are better off with 10 hours or a full BDE course.

Our guide on how many driving lessons you need before your G2 (/blog/how-many-driving-lessons-before-g2/) goes into more detail, including the signs that you are ready to book.

| --- | --- |

| G2 5 hours + road test | $330 + HST ($372.90) |
| G2 10 hours + road test | $550 + HST ($621.50) |

## Should you take the BDE course?

A Ministry-approved BDE course lets you take your G2 road test after 8 months instead of 12, and most insurers offer a discount for new drivers who complete it. Our BDE packages combine online theory with one-on-one in-car lessons in Ajax and the surrounding area. Read whether the BDE course is worth it (/blog/is-bde-course-worth-it/) to decide if it fits your plans.

Many students start lessons near home and then spend their last lesson around the test centre they booked.

Yes. Your instructor picks you up from your home, school or workplace in Ajax and drops you off at the end of the lesson, at no extra charge.

### Can I practise on Highway 401 with a G1?

Only with a certified driving instructor. G1 drivers cannot use 400-series highways with a family member, but highway practice is allowed during a lesson with an instructor certified in Ontario.

Most Ajax drivers take their road test at a nearby centre such as Oshawa or Metro East in Scarborough. Check drivetest.ca for current locations and available dates.

Yes. Every hours plus road test bundle, and the Premium and Advanced BDE packages, include the use of our car on test day along with a warm-up lesson beforehand.

### How soon can I start lessons?

As soon as you have your G1. You can book a single lesson or a bundle without enrolling in the full BDE course.

# Renting a Car for Your Road Test in Ontario: What You Need to Know

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/road-test-car-rental-ontario/
Published: 2026-11-07. Updated: 2026-11-07.

Quick answer: Yes, you can use a rented or driving school car for your Ontario road test, as long as it is in proper working condition, plated and insured, because Ontario's handbook says you must bring a vehicle that meets those standards. If the car fails the examiner's check, the test is declared out-of-order and you lose 50% of your road test fee. At Public Star, our G2 packages with our car for the test start at $200 + HST ($226.00), including lesson time and a warm-up drive.

You booked your road test, and now you need a car. Maybe the family car is not available, has a warning light on, or you just do not want to test in an unfamiliar vehicle. This guide covers what Ontario requires from the car, what happens if it is not ready, your options, and what a driving school car costs in Scarborough and Durham Region.

## Can you use a rented car for your road test in Ontario?

Yes. Ontario does not require you to own the car you take your test in. The Official MTO Driver's Handbook says you must bring "the appropriate vehicle" to your road test, and that it must be fit, in proper working condition, plated and insured.

So a family car, a rental or a driving school car can all work, as long as it meets those standards and you are allowed and insured to drive it. The handbook's advice on choosing a driving school even lists "use of vehicle for road test" as something a school's contract should spell out.

## What the car must have on test day

Before you drive anywhere, the examiner checks the car. Here is what to confirm the day before:

- Valid plates and insurance. The car must be plated and insured, and you should have the ownership and insurance documents in the car.
- Working lights and signals. Headlights, brake lights and every turn signal, front and back.
- Working horn and brakes. Including the parking brake.
- A clean, uncracked view. A windshield crack in your line of sight, or a broken mirror, can be a problem.
- No dashboard warning lights that suggest the car is not safe to drive.
- Working seatbelts for both you and the examiner.
- Enough fuel to finish the test without stopping.

Our list of G2 road test automatic fails (/blog/g2-road-test-automatic-fails/) goes through the car problems that end a test before it starts.

## What happens if the car is not ready

This is the part that catches people out. Ontario's handbook says that if your vehicle does not meet ministry standards for a road test, the examiner declares the test out-of-order. When that happens:

1. You lose 50% of your road test fee.
2. The other 50% stays on your driving record as a credit.
3. To book again, you pay the missing 50% first.

An out-of-order test is not a fail, but you still pay for it and wait for a new date. If you are worried about your car, the handbook says to contact the DriveTest centre before your test.

## Rules that apply no matter whose car it is

A few road test rules from Ontario's handbook affect how you plan the car:

- No passengers. Only you and the examiner can be in the car. Driving instructors, friends, relatives and translators cannot ride along.
- No driving aids. Automatic parallel parking, lane monitoring, cruise control and back cameras may not be used during the test. If you have learned to park with a back camera, practise with mirrors and shoulder checks before test day.
- Arrive at least 30 minutes early. The handbook's checklist says to arrive at least 30 minutes before your appointment.
- Plan your ride home. If you are taking the G2 test on a G1, a fully licensed driver needs to come with you, and if you are taking the G test on a G2, be ready to get home another way in case you do not pass.
- Cancel early if you need to. If you cancel or reschedule with less than 48 hours notice, or miss the test, your prepaid road test fee is not refunded.

## Your options for a road test car

| Option | Good points | Things to check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Family or friend's car | Free, and you may already practise in it | It must pass the vehicle check, the owner's insurance must cover you, and a fully licensed driver may need to come with you |
| Rental company car | Newer car in good condition | Many rental companies have their own age and licence rules, so ask whether a G1 or G2 driver can drive it and how insurance works. Newer cars often have driving aids you will need to switch off or ignore |
| Driving school car | Checked before the test, instructor brings it, warm-up drive included | Book early, since popular test dates and times fill up |

A regular rental can work, but you may be driving an unfamiliar car on the most important drive of the year.

## Why most students use a driving school car

With a driving school package, the car problem disappears. Here is what our road test packages include:

- Our instructor's car for the test, plated, insured and checked before your appointment.
- A warm-up lesson right before the test, so your first drive of the day is not the test itself.
- A car you already know. You practise in the same car during your lessons, so the mirrors, brakes and turning feel familiar.
- Pick-up and drop-off in Scarborough, North York, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa.
- An instructor at the centre who handles the timing, so you can focus on driving.

If you are not sure how much practice you need before the test, read how many driving lessons you need before your G2 test (/blog/how-many-driving-lessons-before-g2/).

## How much does a road test car cost?

Every "road test" package below includes our car for the test plus the lesson hours listed. Prices are before and after 13% HST.

| G2 package | Price |
| --- | --- |
| 1 hour lesson (no road test car) | $50 + HST ($56.50) |
| 2 hours + road test | $200 + HST ($226.00) |
| 3 hours + road test | $250 + HST ($282.50) |
| 4 hours + road test | $300 + HST ($339.00) |
| 5 hours + road test | $330 + HST ($372.90) |
| 10 hours + road test | $550 + HST ($621.50) |

| G package | Price |
| --- | --- |
| 1 hour lesson (no road test car) | $60 + HST ($67.80) |
| 2 hours + road test | $250 + HST ($282.50) |
| 3 hours + road test | $300 + HST ($339.00) |
| 4 hours + road test | $360 + HST ($406.80) |
| 5 hours + road test | $400 + HST ($452.00) |

Our Premium and Advanced BDE packages also include our car for your G2 road test. DriveTest's own road test fee is separate and is paid to DriveTest, not to us. Check the current amount on the DriveTest fee list (https://drivetest.ca/tests/fees/) when you book.

For a full breakdown of lesson and package prices, see our driving lesson cost guide (/blog/driving-lessons-cost-ontario/).

## Tips if you use a rented or borrowed car

1. Drive it once or twice before the test to get used to the brakes and turning circle.
2. Find every control before you arrive: signals, hazards, horn, wipers, defroster and parking brake.
3. Check every light the night before with a helper standing outside the car.
4. Bring the documents: ownership and proof of insurance in the car, plus your licence and glasses or contacts if you need them to drive.

For tips on the drive itself, read how to pass your G2 road test on the first try (/blog/how-to-pass-g2-road-test/), and if you are going for your full licence, our G road test highway tips (/blog/g-road-test-highway-tips/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I use a driving school car for my road test in Ontario?

Yes. A driving school car is a normal choice and Ontario's handbook lists use of a vehicle for the road test as something driving schools may offer. The car must be in proper working condition, plated and insured, like any other test car.

### Can my driving instructor sit in the car during the test?

No. Only you and the examiner can be in the car. Your instructor can drive you to the centre, warm you up and wait for you.

### What happens if my rental car fails the vehicle check?

The examiner declares the test out-of-order. You lose 50% of your road test fee, the other half stays as a credit, and you pay the missing half to book a new test.

### Can I use the back camera in my car during the test?

No. Ontario's handbook says electronic aids such as back cameras, automatic parallel parking, lane monitoring and cruise control may not be used during the road test.

### How much is a road test car rental at Public Star?

Our G2 packages with our car for the test start at $200 + HST ($226.00) for 2 hours plus the road test. G packages start at $250 + HST ($282.50).

# Ontario G1 to G Licence Timeline and Costs: How Long It Takes

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/g1-to-g-licence-timeline-ontario/
Published: 2026-11-06. Updated: 2026-11-06.

Quick answer: In Ontario you hold your G1 for 12 months, or 8 months if you finish a government-approved driver education course, then hold your G2 for 12 months before the G road test. That makes the minimum 20 months with a course or 24 months without, and Ontario says most people take about 20 months. You have up to five years to finish, or you start over. Lessons are optional, and with us G2 lessons start at $50 + HST ($56.50) an hour, while DriveTest's own test and licence fees are listed on drivetest.ca.

Getting a full G licence in Ontario is a two-step process, and the waiting periods matter more than anything else when you plan it. This guide lays out the timeline from your first G1 to your full G, what you can and cannot do at each stage, and what the process can cost. It is written for new drivers in Scarborough, North York, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa, but the rules are the same everywhere in Ontario.

## How long does it take to get a G licence in Ontario?

Ontario says that for most people the two-step process takes about 20 months. Here is how that breaks down, based on the rules on ontario.ca (https://www.ontario.ca/page/get-g-drivers-licence-new-drivers):

| Stage | Minimum time | How you move on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G1 | 12 months, or 8 months with an approved driver education course | Pass the G2 road test (the G1 exit test) |
| G2 | 12 months | Pass the G road test (the G2 exit test) |
| Whole process | 20 months with a course, 24 without | You must finish within 5 years |

So the fastest route is 8 months on a G1 with a government-approved course, then 12 months on a G2: 20 months in total. Without a course, the minimum is 12 plus 12, so plan on at least 24 months from G1 to G.

The five year limit is the one people forget. Ontario says you have up to five years to finish the whole process, and if you do not get your full G licence in that time, you need to start over. If your G2 is getting close to that date, book your G test early so a cancellation or a failed attempt does not push you past it.

## Step 1: getting your G1

You can apply for a driver's licence in Ontario once you are at least 16 years old. You pass a vision test and a knowledge test on the rules of the road and traffic signs at a DriveTest centre, and you pay a fee to apply and take the knowledge test. DriveTest keeps the current amounts on its list of fees (https://drivetest.ca/tests/fees/), so check there before you go.

To study, use the official Driver's Handbook. Ontario lists the printed handbook at $14.95 plus taxes.

### G1 rules you have to follow

Ontario's G1 conditions are strict, and breaking them can cost you your licence:

- Keep a zero blood alcohol level.
- Do not drive between midnight and 5 a.m.
- Do not drive on 400-series highways or high-speed expressways, unless you are with a driving instructor certified in Ontario.
- Always drive with a fully licensed driver who has at least four years of driving experience and a blood alcohol level under .05 (zero if they are 21 or under). They must be the only other person in the front seat.
- Make sure every passenger wears a working seatbelt.

## Should you take a BDE course to shorten the G1 wait?

If you finish a government-approved driver education course, Ontario lets you take your first road test after 8 months instead of 12. That four month head start is the main reason many students choose a Beginner Driver Education (BDE) course, but the training itself matters just as much: you learn defensive driving and test skills from the start instead of picking up habits you later have to unlearn.

Our BDE packages:

| BDE package | Price |
| --- | --- |
| Basic | $499 + HST ($563.87) |
| Premium | $649 + HST ($733.37) |
| Advanced | $799 + HST ($902.87) |

For a closer look at the trade-offs, read is the BDE course worth it (/blog/is-bde-course-worth-it/).

## Step 2: the G2 road test and G2 rules

Once your G1 time is up, you can book the G2 road test. It checks basic driving skills: turns, stops, lane changes, parking and reversing. Our guide on how to pass the G2 road test on the first try (/blog/how-to-pass-g2-road-test/) covers what examiners look for, and how many driving lessons you need before your G2 test (/blog/how-many-driving-lessons-before-g2/) helps you decide how much help to get.

After you pass, you hold a G2 for 12 months. Ontario says G2 drivers can drive on all Ontario roads, at any time of day in most cases, without another experienced driver in the car. A few rules still apply:

- Keep a zero blood alcohol level.
- Carry only as many passengers as there are working seatbelts.
- If you are 19 or under, between midnight and 5 a.m. you can only carry one passenger aged 19 or under during your first six months on a G2, and up to three after that. These limits do not apply if a fully licensed driver with at least four years of experience is in the front seat, or if your passengers are immediate family. Our guide to G2 licence rules and restrictions (/blog/g2-licence-rules-ontario/) covers every G2 condition and the penalties for breaking them.

## Step 3: the G road test

After 12 months on your G2, you can take the G road test. This test is longer and includes highway or expressway driving, so it is worth getting real practice at highway speeds before you book. See our G road test highway tips (/blog/g-road-test-highway-tips/) and the G2 vs G road test (/blog/g2-vs-g-road-test/) comparison to see what changes.

## What does it cost to go from G1 to G?

The total depends on how much help you want. There are two kinds of costs:

1. DriveTest fees, which the government sets: the knowledge test and licence, and each road test. These are the same at every DriveTest centre. We do not repeat the amounts here because they change, so check the current DriveTest fee list (https://drivetest.ca/tests/fees/).
2. Optional training and a test car, which you choose. Ontario does not require any paid lessons.

If you do want lessons or our car for test day, here are our current G2 and G prices. Every "road test" package includes our instructor's car for the test and a warm-up drive first.

| G2 package | Price |
| --- | --- |
| 1 hour lesson | $50 + HST ($56.50) |
| 2 hours + road test | $200 + HST ($226.00) |
| 3 hours + road test | $250 + HST ($282.50) |
| 4 hours + road test | $300 + HST ($339.00) |
| 5 hours + road test | $330 + HST ($372.90) |
| 10 hours + road test | $550 + HST ($621.50) |

| G package | Price |
| --- | --- |
| 1 hour lesson | $60 + HST ($67.80) |
| 2 hours + road test | $250 + HST ($282.50) |
| 3 hours + road test | $300 + HST ($339.00) |
| 4 hours + road test | $360 + HST ($406.80) |
| 5 hours + road test | $400 + HST ($452.00) |

For example, a student who takes our Premium BDE course and later a 3 hours + road test G package would pay $733.37 + $339.00 = $1,072.37 with us, plus DriveTest's own fees. Our driving lesson price guide (/blog/driving-lessons-cost-ontario/) compares more options.

## Tips for keeping your timeline on track

- Book road tests early. Test dates near Scarborough and Durham can fill up, so book as soon as you know when your waiting period ends.
- Count from your licence date. Your 8 or 12 months start when you get the licence, not when you start practising.
- Watch the five year limit. Write down the date your G1 was issued and plan backward from the five year mark.
- New to Canada? If you already hold a licence from another country, read our guide to converting a foreign driver's licence in Ontario (/blog/foreign-licence-exchange-ontario/) first. Your experience may shorten your path.
- Practise between lessons. Waiting periods only help if you actually drive. Regular practice with a licensed family member makes every lesson count more.

## Frequently asked questions

### How long do you have to wait between G1 and G2 in Ontario?

Ontario says you can take your first road test after 12 months with a G1, or after 8 months if you finish a government-approved driver education course.

### How long do you have to wait between G2 and G?

You can take the G road test after 12 months with a G2 licence.

### How long do I have to get my full G licence?

Up to five years from the start of the process. If you do not get your full G in that time, you need to start over.

### Can I drive on the highway with a G1?

Not on 400-series highways or high-speed expressways, unless you are driving with a driving instructor certified in Ontario. G2 drivers can drive on all Ontario roads.

### How much are the DriveTest fees?

DriveTest sets the fees for the knowledge test, licence and road tests, and they can change. Check the current amounts on drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca/tests/fees/) before you book.

# How Many Driving Lessons Do I Need Before My G2 Test?

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/how-many-driving-lessons-before-g2/
Published: 2026-11-05. Updated: 2026-11-05.

Quick answer: Ontario does not set a minimum number of professional lessons for the G2 road test, but you must hold your G1 for 12 months first, or 8 months if you finish a government-approved driver education course. As a rule of thumb, drivers who already practise regularly with a family member usually need 2 to 5 hours with an instructor to fix habits and learn the test, while true beginners are better off with 10 hours or a full BDE course.

"How many lessons do I need?" is the first thing most new drivers ask us. The honest answer is that it depends on how much you have already driven, not on a number set by the government. This guide explains what Ontario actually requires, how to judge where you are, and how many hours make sense for different kinds of drivers in Scarborough, North York, Pickering, Ajax, Whitby and Oshawa.

## Does Ontario require a minimum number of driving lessons?

No. Ontario does not require you to take any professional lessons before your G2 road test (the G1 exit test). What it does require is time:

- You must hold your G1 licence for 12 months before your first road test.
- If you finish a government-approved driver education course, you can take the road test after 8 months.
- You have five years to finish the whole graduated licensing process, or you start over.

So lessons are not a legal box to tick. They are there to get you ready to pass and to drive safely afterwards. If you are thinking about the 8 month option, our guide on whether the BDE course is worth it (/blog/is-bde-course-worth-it/) walks through the trade-offs, and our G1 to G licence timeline (/blog/g1-to-g-licence-timeline-ontario/) shows every step from G1 to your full G.

## How many lessons do most drivers need?

There is no official statistic on this, so we will not invent one. What we can share is a simple guide based on where you are starting from:

| Your situation | Suggested lessons with an instructor |
| --- | --- |
| You drive several times a week with a family member and feel confident | 2 to 3 hours, focused on test skills |
| You practise sometimes but still hesitate at left turns or lane changes | 4 to 5 hours |
| You have barely driven, or you are very nervous | 10 hours, or a full BDE course |
| You failed a previous G2 test | 2 to 3 hours on the items on your scoresheet |

These are starting points. Your instructor will tell you after the first lesson whether you need more or less.

## Signs you are ready for the G2 road test

Hours matter less than skills. Before you book, you should be able to do all of these smoothly, without someone in the passenger seat reminding you:

1. Full stops behind the line at every stop sign, then a clear look both ways.
2. Mirror, signal, shoulder check before every lane change and every pull-out from the curb.
3. Left turns at busy lights, waiting in the intersection for a safe gap.
4. Parallel parking and a three-point turn on a quiet street.
5. Residential driving at a steady speed, watching for pedestrians and parked cars.
6. Keeping a safe following distance in traffic.

Ontario lists these skills on its G2 road test page: left and right turns, stopping, parallel parking, one-way streets, lane changes, three-point turns, residential neighbourhoods, and traffic lights, stop and yield signs. If any of them still feels shaky, that is where your lessons should go.

For a full test-day checklist, read how to pass your G2 road test on the first try (/blog/how-to-pass-g2-road-test/).

## Why practice with family is not always enough

Practising with a parent or friend is a great way to build hours behind the wheel. The catch is that family members often pass on habits that cost marks on a road test, such as rolling stops, skipped shoulder checks, or one hand on the wheel. They also may not know what examiners look for.

A few lessons with a certified instructor help you:

- Spot and fix bad habits before they become automatic.
- Learn the test format, including how the examiner gives directions.
- Practise on roads like those near your test centre, since DriveTest does not publish its routes.
- Avoid automatic fails, like the ones in our G2 road test automatic fails list (/blog/g2-road-test-automatic-fails/).

One more benefit: Ontario lets a G1 driver with a certified driving instructor drive on any road, so lessons are also a chance to try roads you cannot use with a family member.

## Should you book lessons all at once or spread them out?

Spread them out if you can. One or two lessons a week, with family practice in between, works better than five hours crammed into the week of your test. You get time to practise what the instructor taught you, then come back and fix what is still not right.

A good plan for most drivers looks like this:

- First lesson: a full assessment, so you know exactly what to work on.
- Middle lessons: focus on your weak spots, such as parking or busy intersections.
- Last lesson: a mock road test, then a warm-up drive on test day.

## How much do G2 lessons cost?

These are our current G2 prices. HST is 13%, and the total is shown in brackets.

| G2 package | Price |
| --- | --- |
| 1 hour lesson | $50 + HST ($56.50) |
| 2 hours + road test | $200 + HST ($226.00) |
| 3 hours + road test | $250 + HST ($282.50) |
| 4 hours + road test | $300 + HST ($339.00) |
| 5 hours + road test | $330 + HST ($372.90) |
| 10 hours + road test | $550 + HST ($621.50) |

The road test packages include a warm-up before your test and the use of our instructor's car for the test itself, so you do not need to worry about a family car failing the vehicle check. The DriveTest road test fee is separate and paid to DriveTest. Check the current amount on drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca/tests/fees/).

If you want the 8 month option, our BDE packages are:

| BDE package | Price |
| --- | --- |
| Basic | $499 + HST ($563.87) |
| Premium | $649 + HST ($733.37) |
| Advanced | $799 + HST ($902.87) |

For a full breakdown, see our driving lesson price guide (/blog/driving-lessons-cost-ontario/).

## What if you are taking your test at a busy centre?

Many of our students test at Metro East in Scarborough or at the Oshawa centre. Both have busy roads nearby, so it helps to spend at least one lesson in that area. Our guides to Metro East DriveTest (/blog/metro-east-drivetest-tips/) and Oshawa DriveTest (/blog/oshawa-drivetest-tips/) describe the kinds of roads you can expect.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is 2 hours of driving lessons enough for the G2 test?

It can be, if you already drive often and confidently with a family member. Two hours is usually enough to fix a few habits and run through the test. If you are still unsure about parking or busy intersections, book more.

### Can I take the G2 test without any lessons?

Yes. Ontario does not require professional lessons. You only need to hold your G1 for 12 months, or 8 months with an approved driver education course.

### How many lessons do I need if I have never driven before?

Start with an assessment lesson. Most complete beginners need around 10 hours with an instructor, plus regular practice, before they are ready. A BDE course is also a good fit and can shorten your G1 wait to 8 months.

### Do lessons have to be with a certified instructor?

To count toward the 8 month option, you need to finish a government-approved driver education course. Ontario lists approved driving schools on ontario.ca. Practice with a fully licensed family member does not shorten the wait.

### When should I take my last lesson?

Ideally within a few days of your test, followed by a warm-up drive on the day itself. That keeps the skills fresh without leaving you tired.

# Oshawa DriveTest: Road Test Tips for the Midtown Mall Centre

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/oshawa-drivetest-tips/
Published: 2026-11-04. Updated: 2026-11-04.

Quick answer: Oshawa DriveTest is in Midtown Mall at 200 John St W, Oshawa, and it runs road test appointments Monday to Saturday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The G2 road test costs $53.75 and the G road test costs $91.25, and DriveTest asks you to arrive at least 30 minutes early. The best preparation is practising on the busy downtown streets, residential roads and highway ramps around the centre so nothing on test day feels new.

Oshawa is the main DriveTest centre for drivers in Durham Region. Many of our students from Oshawa, Whitby, Ajax and Pickering book their G2 or G test there because it is close to home and they can practise on the same kinds of roads. This guide covers the practical side: where the centre is, when road tests run, what they cost, what happens after you check in, and how to get ready for driving in that part of Oshawa.

## Where is the Oshawa DriveTest centre?

DriveTest lists the centre as Oshawa at:

Midtown Mall, 200 John St W, Oshawa, L1J 2B4

The centre is inside a mall, so you park in the lot and walk in to check in. Leave extra time if you are driving in from Whitby, Ajax or Pickering. Highway 401 and the main east to west roads can back up at rush hour, and arriving late and rushed is a bad way to start a road test.

## Oshawa DriveTest hours and road tests offered

DriveTest's centre list shows Oshawa as a full-time centre that offers a wide range of road tests, including G2 and G for cars, M2 and M for motorcycles, and commercial classes.

| Service | Days | Hours |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inside services (licences, knowledge tests) | Monday to Friday | 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. |
| Road test appointments | Monday to Saturday | 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. |

Hours can change for holidays or bad weather, so check the DriveTest service disruptions page (https://drivetest.ca/find-a-drivetest-centre/service-disruptions/) on the morning of your test. DriveTest also notes that the G road test has been temporarily modified at full-time centres, so read the current G test description on drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca/tests/road-tests-cars/) before you book.

## How much does a road test in Oshawa cost?

Road test fees are the same at every DriveTest centre in Ontario. These are DriveTest's current fees:

| Road test | DriveTest fee |
| --- | --- |
| Class G2 road test | $53.75 |
| Class G road test | $91.25 |

If you cancel or reschedule with less than 48 hours notice, or do not show up, you lose your road test fee. You can book and pay for G2 and G tests online. Always confirm the latest amounts on drivetest.ca (https://drivetest.ca/tests/fees/) before you book.

## What happens on test day in Oshawa

The process is the same at every DriveTest centre. Knowing it ahead of time takes a lot of the nerves away.

1. Arrive at least 30 minutes early. DriveTest asks for this at every centre.
2. Park and go inside to check in. Bring your licence and be ready to confirm your booking.
3. Go back to your car and wait. The examiner comes to you in the parking lot.
4. Vehicle check. Before you drive, the examiner checks that the car is safe. Lights, signals, horn, brakes, tires and the windshield all matter.
5. The drive. DriveTest says the G2 test usually takes about 20 minutes.
6. Results. The examiner gives you a short summary at the end along with your scoresheet.

A few rules catch people out:

- No passengers. Your instructor, friends and family cannot ride along. Only you and the examiner are in the car.
- No recording. Phones and dashboard cameras must be off during the test.
- No driving aids. Features such as automatic parking, lane keeping, cruise control and back cameras may not be used during the test. Practise parking with your mirrors and shoulder checks.
- Plan your ride home. If you take your G2 test on a G1, you cannot drive home alone if you do not pass, so bring a fully licensed driver or arrange another ride.

For the car problems and driving errors that end a test early, see our list of G2 road test automatic fails (/blog/g2-road-test-automatic-fails/).

## How to prepare for the roads around Oshawa DriveTest

DriveTest does not publish its test routes, and examiners can take you anywhere nearby. Instead of memorising one route, get comfortable with the kinds of roads you will meet around downtown Oshawa:

- Downtown streets. Expect traffic lights close together, buses, pedestrians and cars pulling in and out of parking spots. Some downtown streets are one-way, so read every sign and stay in the correct lane before you turn.
- Busy arterial roads. Multi-lane roads in Oshawa carry heavy traffic and lots of turning cars. Do a mirror check, signal and shoulder check for every lane change.
- Left turns at busy lights. Move into the intersection when it is safe, wait for a real gap, and turn into the correct lane. Never rush a left turn because someone behind you is impatient.
- Residential streets. Quiet side streets mean stop signs, school zones, parked cars and people walking. Stop fully behind the line, look both ways, and watch your speed.
- Leaving and entering the mall lot. Your test starts and ends in a parking lot. Drive slowly, watch for pedestrians, and signal when you pull onto the road.
- Parking and reversing. The G2 test checks parking and reversing, so practise until it feels routine.

If you are taking the G test, add highway practice on Highway 401 and Highway 407 ramps if you can. Our G road test highway tips (/blog/g-road-test-highway-tips/) cover merging, lane changes at speed and exits, and our G2 vs G road test guide (/blog/g2-vs-g-road-test/) explains how the two tests differ.

## Should you take your test in Oshawa or somewhere else?

There is no official ranking of "easy" DriveTest centres, and we will not make one up. Every centre uses the same scoring standards. The better question is which centre's roads you can practise on the most. If you live in Oshawa, Whitby or Courtice, Oshawa is usually the most convenient choice. Students in Scarborough often prefer Metro East DriveTest (/blog/metro-east-drivetest-tips/), and some in Pickering and Ajax book Port Union. Pick the centre near where you can get real practice, then book early, because test dates can fill up.

For general advice that works at any centre, read how to pass your G2 road test on the first try (/blog/how-to-pass-g2-road-test/).

# Metro East DriveTest: Road Test Tips for the Scarborough Area Centre

URL: https://publicstardrivingschool.com/blog/metro-east-drivetest-tips/
Published: 2026-11-03. Updated: 2026-11-03.

Quick answer: Metro East DriveTest is at Victoria Terrace Plaza, 1448 Lawrence Ave E, Unit 15, Toronto, and it runs G2 and G road tests Monday to Saturday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The G2 road test costs $53.75 and the G road test costs $91.25, and DriveTest asks you to arrive at least 30 minutes early. The best preparation is practising on the busy arterial roads and residential streets around the centre so nothing on test day is new to you.

Metro East is one of the busiest DriveTest centres for drivers from Scarborough, North York and East York. Lots of our students book their G2 or G test there because it is close to home. This guide covers the practical side: where it is, when road tests run, what it costs, what happens after you check in, and how to prepare for driving in that part of the city.

## Where is the Metro East DriveTest centre?

DriveTest lists the centre as Toronto Metro East at:

Victoria Terrace Plaza, 1448 Lawrence Ave E, Unit 15, Toronto, M4A 2V6

It sits in a plaza on Lawrence Avenue East, so you park in the plaza lot and walk in to check in. If you are coming from Scarborough, Pickering or Ajax, give yourself extra time: Lawrence and the roads that feed into it can be slow at rush hour, and you do not want to start your test already stressed about being late.

## Metro East hours and road tests offered

According to DriveTest's centre list, Metro East offers road tests for classes G2, G, M2 and M.

| Service | Days | Hours |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inside services (licences, knowledge tests) | Monday to Friday | 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. |
| Inside services | Saturday | 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. |
| Road test appointments | Monday to Saturday | 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. |

Hours can change for holidays or bad weather, so check the DriveTest service disruptions page (https://drivetest.ca/find-a-drivetest-centre/service-disruptions/) on the morning of your test.

| Road test | DriveTest fee |

| Class G road test | $91.25 |
